title: Mountains
source: After the notes' South America and Africa physical maps, with standard UPSC facts added

places.name: Andes
places.significance: The longest mountain range on Earth: young fold mountains running the whole Pacific edge of South America through seven countries
notes: The longest mountain range in the world, about 7,000 km
Runs through Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina — 7 countries

places.name: Cordillera Oriental
places.significance: The Andes' eastern range in the north, carrying Bogotá's plateau up through Colombia into Venezuela
notes: Mainly in Colombia, a small part in Venezuela

places.name: Cotopaxi
places.significance: One of the highest active volcanoes on Earth, a perfect snow cone on the avenue of volcanoes south of Quito

places.name: Chimborazo
places.significance: Ecuador's highest peak, whose summit — on the Equator's bulge — is the farthest point on Earth from its centre

places.name: Huascarán
places.significance: Peru's highest peak and the highest in the tropics, crowning the Cordillera Blanca

places.name: Misti
places.significance: The snow-capped cone that looms over Arequipa

places.name: Ojos del Salado
places.significance: The highest active volcano on Earth, on the Argentina–Chile border above the Atacama

places.name: Aconcagua
places.significance: The highest peak of South America — and of the world outside Asia — near the Argentina–Chile border
notes: The highest peak of South America, 6,961 m
In Argentina's Mendoza province, close to the border with Chile

places.name: Atlas Mountains
places.significance: Young fold mountains along Africa's north-west edge, from the Atlantic coast of Morocco to Tunisia
notes: Run through Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia
Highest peak: Toubkal (4,167 m), in Morocco
They keep the Mediterranean's rain from the desert to the south

places.name: Hoggar Mountains
places.significance: A volcanic highland in the heart of the great desert, in southern Algeria around Tamanrasset

places.name: Tibesti Mountains
places.significance: The great desert's highest mountains, a volcanic massif in northern Chad on the Libyan border
notes: Highest point: Emi Koussi (3,445 m), the highest of the Sahara

places.name: Drakensberg
places.significance: The high eastern rim of southern Africa's plateau, rising over 3,000 m above the Indian Ocean coast
notes: Old, residual mountains — the eroded edge of the plateau, the Great Escarpment
Highest point: Thabana Ntlenyana (3,482 m), in Lesotho

places.name: Kilimanjaro
places.significance: Africa's highest peak, 5,895 m — a free-standing volcano on the plains of northern Tanzania
notes: The highest peak of Africa: 5,895 m (Uhuru Peak)
A volcano — the notes call it extinct; its outer cones are, while Kibo, the summit cone, is dormant

places.name: Mount Kenya
places.significance: Africa's second-highest peak, 5,199 m — an old volcano standing just south of the Equator
notes: The second highest peak of Africa: 5,199 m (Batian)
An extinct volcano, just south of the Equator

places.name: Mount Cameroon
places.significance: West Africa's highest peak, an active volcano rising straight from the shore of the Gulf of Guinea
notes: An active volcano — one of Africa's most active, it erupted in 1999 and 2000
About 4,040 m, the highest of West Africa

places.name: Ras Dashen
places.significance: Ethiopia's highest peak, about 4,550 m, in the Simien Mountains north-east of Lake Tana
notes: The highest peak of Ethiopia, in the Simien Mountains
